NEW scoped AC4-SUMMON-TARGET-01: while this finite body exists, mechanically eligible as an active creature and living ally for ordinary HP-healing/living-creature targeting, including Cleric Healing Rite. No natural origin, biology, soul, corpse, undead/construct or cosmological identity is inferred.

NEW scoped AC4-SUMMON-TARGET-01: solely for the two authored AC4 temporary profiles Summon Water Pet and Faction Envoy, while their finite body exists they count as an active creature and as a living ally for ordinary HP-healing/living-creature targeting, including Cleric Healing Rite. This is a mechanical targeting classification only; it establishes no natural origin, biology, soul, corpse, loot, undead/construct taxonomy or cosmological identity. Null Disabled 0 remains the same existing body and may receive an otherwise legal heal; an ended/expired/dismissed body is no longer a target. Resonance Beacon uses active-creature identity rather than biological 'living' status: an enrolled creature must still be able to spend its own Action and RP.

changes.before: One-minute concentration effects use the source's normal ten future caster regular-start markers in initiative or 60 elapsed seconds outside unless this card states a different exact clock. Ten minutes = 100 future caster regular-start markers or 600 elapsed seconds. Alignment Lock uses 24 elapsed hours; rank-7 Alignment Anchor uses seven elapsed days; Bind Element uses two future target regular ends / 12 elapsed seconds outside initiative. Preserve virtual/absolute deadlines through initiative changes, absence and suppression.
changes.after:
One-minute concentration effects use the source's normal ten future caster regular-start markers in initiative or 60 elapsed seconds outside unless this card states a different exact clock. Ten minutes = 100 future caster regular-start markers or 600 elapsed seconds. Alignment Lock uses 24 elapsed hours; rank-7 Alignment Anchor uses seven elapsed days; Bind Element uses two future target regular ends / 12 elapsed seconds outside initiative. SPELL SHIELD EXACT CLOCK — Because Spell Shield is nonconcentration, its own one-minute deadline is explicit: in initiative, application records the caster's tenth future regular-start marker after application, excluding any start already in progress or past. Outside initiative, deadline = application timestamp + 60 elapsed seconds. Preserve that fixed virtual/absolute deadline across initiative entry/exit, reorder, extra turns, absence, caster death and suppression. Caster death alone does not end Spell Shield.

changes.before:
Action; range 60 feet; V/S/F. NEW: replace Instantaneous protection metadata with one minute, without concentration, on one willing perceived creature with line of effect. Only one pending Spell Shield can protect a recipient across casters; a successful replacement ends the prior one. Interpret 3rd level and Tier 3 as the triggering spell’s actual generating rank 0–3. Caster level, discounted RP price and target class do not determine eligibility. After ordinary interruption and before any original attack, save or payload resolution, the recipient may spend its Reaction to reflect a hostile pending spell whose only selected creature target is that recipient. The reflected path originates at the protected recipient and ends at the original caster, who must fit the original spell’s creature-type, willingness, range and line-of-effect requirements measured from that return origin. Hidden eligibility is adjudicated without disclosing protected information. Revalidate, then spend the Reaction and consume the shield. Redirect the one payload, retaining the original caster’s ownership, statistics, costs, concentration and causal identity. Resolve its normal attack or save against that caster, with no automatic self-hit or duplicate roll against the former target. Areas, multiple targets, nonspells, copies and already reflected packets are ineligible. A declined or ineligible event leaves the shield available until its original deadline. No legal return target means no reflection. Suppression disables triggering while its timer continues. It cannot reflect its own creation or initiate another reflection/copy chain.

CURRENT INTERFACE — Spell Shield is a pure redirection of the already-pending original spell payload, not a new reflected/retaliatory damage root. The original cast ID, generating rank, caster ownership, attack/save statistics, concentration owner, source costs, and any creation-time Null `nullNonlethal` flag remain unchanged. The protected recipient is only the return origin for range/line-of-effect revalidation. If the returned spell creates an ongoing target branch or delayed rider, that branch/rider is attached to the original caster as its new recipient while retaining the original spell/caster identity. Because no new damage root is created, a Veiled reflector does not newly make the returned damage Null-nonlethal, and an un-Veiled reflector does not strip an original Veiled caster's root flag. The packet cannot trigger Spell Shield again and cannot be copied/reflected recursively.

changes.before:
Action; range 60 feet; V/S/F; concentration up to one minute. Create one Medium Elemental companion in a perceived fitting unoccupied supported space with line of effect. Preserve printed AC 14, HP 35, 2d6 healing and 1d10 cold attack. NEW profile: walking Speed 30 feet, body mass 150 pounds, all six ability scores 10, saves equal to your PB, other checks +0, ordinary sight/hearing. It understands your spoken commands without speech or telepathy. No swimming, amphibious trait, fluid passage, immunity or free water follows from its name. It acts immediately after your regular turn. A Bonus Action command while within 60 feet and able to perceive you permits movement and one attack, heal, Dodge, Dash, Disengage or Search. Without a command it can move defensively and Dodge. No free Help, grapple, shove, item activation or opportunity attack is granted. Attack: one melee spell attack using your actual casting ability + PB, reach 5 feet, 1d10 cold without a modifier. Heal: one willing living creature it perceives within 5 feet and line of effect regains 2d6 ordinary HP without a modifier. A Downed recipient is eligible under its actual healing rules. NEW: either attack or heal consumes the owner’s one shared companion offensive/support activation for that numbered round. One companion therefore cannot heal while another uses that same offensive allowance. Each command still costs its actual Bonus Action; extra turns or repeated commands add no activations. Healing belongs to the pet, without triggering the owner’s personal spell, lifesteal or class hooks; no healing copy, resource conversion or overflow is added. One Water Pet per caster; successful replacement ends the old body. At 0 HP or source end it vanishes without a corpse, loot, death reward or material water. It can carry genuinely entrusted existing gear within its actual capacity; real cargo drops legally on ending. Suppression preserves the existing body/HP and deadline without movement, attack, healing or a fresh summon trigger until resumption.

CURRENT NULL/LIFECYCLE INTERFACE — A qualifying `nullNonlethal=true` damage root that reduces this finite summoned companion from positive HP to 0 does not end or replace the body. Independent concentration end, duration expiry, dismissal or replacement still ends the body. Only a real healing/repair source whose targeting expressly applies to this creature can raise it above 0 and end Disabled; no generic free heal, resummon refresh, or corpse/loot is created.
NEW scoped command decision: its printed 2d6 heal deliberately spends the owner's one shared companion offensive/support activation for that numbered round, the same allowance its attack would spend. Pure movement/Dodge without that heal/attack does not spend the offensive/support allowance beyond the ordinary Bonus Action command.

Initial state: Wizard A (class 7, PB3, INT+4, spell DC15, RP20) bears unsuppressed Null Veil and casts operational Acid Arrow (rank2, base3 RP) at creature B, who already has one pending Spell Shield. B and A are 20 ft apart with line of effect; B has a Reaction. A commits Acid Arrow: RP20→17, Dissonance/Refrain update, and the cast survives interruption. Before the Acid Arrow attack, B spends its Reaction and Spell Shield. Return legality from B to A is valid within Acid Arrow's 30-ft range. The same Acid Arrow cast/root is redirected; A remains caster/dealer/owner and its root keeps nullNonlethal=true because A was Veiled when the root was created. Roll the returned attack against A; on a hit with 4d4=10 and A at 8 HP, qualifying Null damage reduces A to Stable0 rather than creating damage-caused death/Wounds. If the delayed 2d4 Acid Arrow rider attaches, it is still A's original spell branch on A and inherits the same root flag and original deadline rules; it is not a second reflected root. Shield is consumed; no second target receives the original payload.

Initial state: Wizard A is un-Veiled, RP20, concentrating on no spell. B is Veiled and has pending Spell Shield plus a Reaction. A casts operational Charm Person (rank1, base2 RP, concentration up to1 minute) at B from 20 ft. At cast commitment A pays 2 RP and establishes Charm Person concentration before the reaction window. B reflects. The return from B to A is legal and uses A's original spell DC and ownership. B's Veil creates no new Null root because Spell Shield is redirection, not new damage. A remains the concentration owner even though A is now the returned target; if A fails its WIS save the same Charm Person branch affects A under its own odd-but-legal self-target result until its normal ending. Reflection neither transfers concentration to B nor opens a second cast/price/Refrain event.

Initial state: target T has underlying Lawful Good. Caster L (Abjuration rank4) casts Alignment Lock, pays 7 RP, T fails CHA, and L snapshots Lawful/Good until +24h. Later caster P casts reviewed Alignment Purge, pays17 RP, T fails WIS, and Purge's 60-second concentration record becomes live below the lock. Effective read remains Lawful Good because AC4-ALIGN-01 applies Lock last. Then caster S casts a new reviewed Alignment Suggestion. Its target baseline excludes prior Suggestion/Purge overlays under AP-AS-01 and excludes the AC4 Lock overlay under AC4-ALIGN-01; it therefore computes from lawful underlying history, not the locked display, so no staircase occurs. If Suggestion validly establishes an axis change it remains live below Lock. At +30s Purge ends: Lock still displays Lawful Good. At +60s Suggestion ends: Lock still displays Lawful Good. At +24h Lock ends and the then-current underlying lawful record appears. No ended snapshot is restored.

Initial state: target T is under reviewed Purge, so effective alignment is Neutral/Neutral while underlying record is Chaotic Good. A Conjuration rank4 Alignment Anchor zone is created for 7 RP; T is inside at creation and its first zone snapshot is Neutral/Neutral. Purge later ends, but while T stays in the zone the Anchor still freezes Neutral/Neutral. T exits: the zone constraint becomes inactive and underlying Chaotic Good is effective. T reenters the same zone: it reuses that application's original Neutral/Neutral snapshot rather than taking a new snapshot. A separate later Alignment Lock can coexist by its own timestamp; earliest active eligible lock per axis governs among same-family locks. A creature whose moral axis is genuinely undefined entering the zone receives no fabricated Neutral value on that axis. All casts keep their real costs/deadlines regardless of hidden eligibility.

Initial state: caster C has actual invocation permission for canonical faction F and creates Protection-mode Faction Sanctuary, paying7 RP and concentrating up to10 minutes. Owner O is a genuine member of F. O's temporary Faction Envoy stands inside the sanctuary, but its summon record grants only temporary faction affiliation, not institutional membership. Result: O can receive the +2 AC benefit if O personally occupies the area; the Envoy receives no member-only benefit unless an independent actual membership record for that exact body exists. O's positive standing or membership cannot be borrowed by the Envoy. No membership fact is publicly disclosed by the failed benefit.

Initial state: Water Pet is at 6/35 HP with 24 seconds left on its caster's concentration. An enemy damage root was created by a currently Veiled dealer and deals 8 qualifying damage. Pet reaches0 and uses the accepted finite-summon Null branch: same Pet becomes Null Disabled0, Speed0, Incapacitated, no commands/actions; it does not vanish and concentration continues. The Water Pet card itself supplies no self-heal and its 2d6 heal does not automatically establish that this Elemental is a 'living ally' for Healing Rite, so no generic heal is invented. If an independently legal source expressly able to heal this Elemental later restores positive HP, Disabled ends on that actual recovery. In this fixture none does; at the original +24s concentration deadline the same Disabled body independently ends. No corpse, water stock, loot or resummon refund appears.

Initial state: one multiclass owner controls a Water Pet and another companion; both are ready, owner has one Bonus Action and the ordinary one shared damaging/support activation for numbered round 5. Owner spends the Bonus Action commanding Water Pet to heal ally R; roll2d6=7 and R regains7 subject to normal cap. By the AC4 scoped rule that heal spends the owner's one shared support/offense activation for round5. The second companion cannot then make its damaging attack in round5 even if another effect could issue it a command; an extra turn does not refresh the numbered-round allowance. Conversely, if the second companion had attacked first, Water Pet could still move/Dodge under a legal command but could not use its heal that round.

Field is active. Caster A has RP10 and final Resonance Influence Ease. A casts a rank4 spell whose ordinary price is7 with no other modifier: field adds2→9, Ease applies last→8; A may commit if able. Caster B has an exact source waiver reducing a genuine RP-priced spell's ordinary price to0; field mandatory extra makes2, Ease makes1, so a positive payment remains unless the waiver expressly covers mandatory extras. Caster C activates a genuine spell whose normal source cost is one charge and no RP; the AC4 field adds a new2-RP interface while the charge is still spent; with no Influence it costs charge+2 RP. Caster D has no RP pool, so cannot commit that positive2 payment. Oracle E uses a Revelation Charge feature that is not classified as a spell: field adds nothing, because no spell cast occurs. Ongoing concentration pulses and readied-spell release are not new casts and are not recharged.

Initial state: an operational Planar Steed with willing rider has already committed its Planar Crossing Action and required costs/command; origin is outside the future Anchor. Before the crossing resolves, another caster legally establishes Dimensional Anchor so the planned destination footprint lies inside its60-ft sphere. At resolution the whole mount+rider+carried gear transaction fails atomically and remains at origin; no body/cargo splits and committed costs are not refunded. Separate control: two same-plane teleport endpoints both lie outside a Dimensional Anchor while the straight imaginary line between them crosses its sphere. Because Anchor tests actual origin/destination footprints rather than an imagined path, that outside-to-outside transaction is not blocked by this field alone.

Barrier is a30x10 selective plane. A carrier physically carries a genuinely Corrupted passenger toward it. Because the passenger's occupied body would cross, the barrier stops the crossing at the boundary and triggers that passenger's first contact packet for the numbered round; CON save is rolled for that passenger. Later an unsupported Corrupted creature falls through the plane: barrier does not provide support, so it takes one eligible contact packet and the ordinary fall continues beyond the plane. A third Corrupted traveler teleports from one legal space to a fitting destination wholly beyond the barrier without destination overlap; there is no physical path test, so Corruption Barrier alone does not block that teleport. Each creature's one contact entitlement uses its own numbered-round/six-second interval; no standing-near tick is added.

Target E has an actual Elemental creature-type record and is perceived at40 ft. Caster C has already spent its shared character→E hard-denial allowance earlier this encounter. C casts Bind Element anyway, pays7 RP, E fails WIS. The new Paralyzed hard component is blocked by the already-spent guard; no Restrained/Stunned/soft fallback is invented and the paid cast is not refunded. Control variant: with an unused guard, failure establishes Paralyzed through E's second future regular end; at first future end E fails the repeat WIS save, then the effect is suppressed for one interval. Suppression does not pause or restart the second-turn marker. At the second scheduled regular end the application expires even if still suppressed; restoration afterward cannot reapply it for free.

Caster creates one Crystalline Barrier and pays7 RP; wall starts AC18/40HP with original one-minute concentration deadline. Object-legal attacks deal13 total damage, leaving27HP. The wall is then suppressed; a Medium creature moves into part of the former footprint. Suppression does not heal or reset HP. Before the footprint clears, the original concentration deadline arrives and the spell expires. Result: no wall resumes, no creature is evicted/crushed, no 27-HP renewed wall is banked, and no elemental-glass crafting stock or shards are created.

Recipient R has Greater Warding, Warding Bond to ally B, and3 temp HP. A spell-origin packet deals11 damage before defenses. Greater Warding resistance halves once: floor(11/2)=5. Warding Bond then performs its lawful transfer using the already-mitigated packet under its own conserved split; the transferred share cannot be halved again by R's Greater Warding or by treating the transfer as new spell damage. Apply each recipient's temp HP only to the actual share it receives. Greater Warding and Warding Bond retain separate concentration/source endpoints; +2 and +1 same-stat save/AC bonuses use the strongest +2 rather than +3. No absorption/reflection occurs.

Caster C pays7 RP and commits Elemental Drain. One element draw is4=lightning and the single3d6 roll is11. Target U is an active creature-classified Undead with current RP7 and no relevant immunity; it fails CON, takes11 ordinary lightning subject to its defenses, then loses min(5,7)=5 RP→2. Target D is a true dead body/corpse, not an active creature: it is not an active RP holder and cannot lose RP; do not infer creature status from the word undead. Target I is an active eligible creature with RP6 and lightning immunity; on failed CON it takes0 lightning but still loses5 RP→1 because damage immunity does not itself cancel the separate resource-loss branch. C gains no RP and no target goes negative.

Beacon is active on a fixed support. Enrolled traveler T within500 ft spends its Action and2 RP to activate transit while the arrival square is initially legal.
